flows.narrative: Lipper's week-to-19-Aug data shows broad-based inflows: global equity funds +$22.01bn (US +$11.72bn, Europe +$4.70bn, Asia +$2.96bn, EM +$1.57bn -- EM's 6th consecutive week of inflows), bond funds +$15.42bn (20th straight weekly inflow), money-market funds +$3.71bn (a three-week-low pace even as absolute money-market assets remain near record highs, $7.93tn per ICI), and gold funds +$2.04bn (6th straight week) alongside physical gold ETFs +$6.4bn/+46.7 tonnes the week ended ~21 Aug -- strongest gold-ETF inflow in 10 months. A fresher cross-check via BofA/EPFR's Flow Show (week ended ~20 Aug, reported by Bloomberg 21 Aug) shows the same broad-based pattern at larger EPFR-scope magnitudes: global equity funds +$40.1bn (largest in three weeks) and bonds +$21.4bn, with Hartnett's Bull & Bear Indicator at 9.3 ('excessively bullish') and continued 'Anything But Dollar' gold-over-USD positioning -- the two providers aren't directly reconcilable (different universe/methodology) but agree directionally. Notable: BofA's Fund Manager Survey (7-13 Aug poll) showed allocators' cash allocation at 3.5% of AUM, the 6th-lowest ever, even as absolute cash balances sit at records -- a genuine 'low relative cash, high absolute cash' divergence.
